source.title: Understanding Memorization using Representation Similarity Analysis and Model Stitching
source.authors: Aishwarya Gupta; Indranil Saha; Piyush Rai; Marco Fumero; C. Dominé; Zorah Lähner; Donato Crisostomi; Luca Moschella; K. Stachenfeld

record.tranche_reason: The study compares clean and partially label-randomized models using representation similarity and model stitching, then reports test-accuracy changes. It does not use the original versions’ specified measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports stitched-model test-accuracy results and qualitative CKA comparisons. It gives no exact stitched-model test-accuracy values in the supplied text; the figure curves are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation similarity and stitched-model accuracy under partial label corruption. It does not report random-label training fit or the natural-versus-random held-out comparison required by V1, and its experiments do not measure any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors find slower convergence and greater clean-versus-noisy representation differences in deeper layers as label noise increases. They interpret the asymmetric stitching results as suggesting that earlier-layer differences may cascade into deeper layers, so fixing only the final layers may be insufficient to mitigate memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses partial label randomization, CKA comparisons, and model stitching to study layer representations and test performance; it does not reproduce the specified versions’ experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects vary with noise ratio and with how many layers or blocks are stitched.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy-model early layers transfer into clean models with little accuracy loss; including deeper noisy layers produces larger losses as label noise increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional compatibility between clean and partially label-corrupted networks depends on replacement depth and label-noise level.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing only the earliest layers of noisy models with clean-model layers gives no improvement; replacement through roughly half the depth improves accuracy, and further replacement can recover clean-model performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovering clean-model accuracy through model stitching can require replacing layers extending beyond the earliest layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the II edition of the Workshop on Unifying Representations in Neural Models (UniReps 2024)
record.problems: Stitched-model performance is described qualitatively in the text; exact values are only plotted. The supplied text refers to supplementary training details that are not included.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for every plotted noise-ratio and stitch-depth combination: Figure 2 results are described in aggregate in the text, and exact figure values are not reconstructed. CKA findings in Figures 1 and 3 are not rows for the listed versions’ measures.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label training fit, strong natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The text provides qualitative stitching results but no readable numerical figure values or random-label training-fit measurements. The omitted CKA findings are declared in rows_left_out and do not measure any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report that the same architectures and recipes fit fixed random labels nearly perfectly, or compare held-out accuracy under fully random versus natural labels.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank training–test gaps against other measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: CNN model trained on SVHN
rows.stage_stated: trained on SVHN with varied fractions of randomly labeled training examples
rows.operation_detail: Stitched the first k layers of a noisy model to the latter layers of a noise-free model; evaluated test accuracy.

conditions.value: up to every convolution and linear layer

rows.baseline: noise-free model test performance (black dotted line in Figure 2)
rows.value: Stitching early layers results in only a marginal drop; accuracy drops substantially with more noisy layers, proportional to noise r.
rows.note: The text gives qualitative findings, not exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The qualitative accuracy description is supported, but stitched-model accuracy does not establish a listed version. Specify that source-model weights are frozen and only the added stitching layer is trained on clean data.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 model trained on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with varied fractions of randomly labeled training examples
rows.operation_detail: Stitched the first k residual blocks of a noisy model to the latter blocks of a noise-free model; evaluated test accuracy.
rows.baseline: noise-free model test performance (black dotted line in Figure 2)
rows.value: Stitching early blocks results in only a marginal drop; accuracy drops substantially with more noisy blocks, proportional to noise r.
rows.note: The text gives qualitative findings, not exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The qualitative accuracy description is supported, but it does not establish a listed version. Section 3.2 additionally says that including noisy blocks through roughly half the depth causes no substantial degradation. Only the added stitching layer is trained on clean data.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 model trained on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with varied fractions of randomly labeled training examples
rows.operation_detail: Stitched noise-free model layers up to the second residual block to the deeper layers of a noisy model; evaluated test accuracy.

conditions.value: up to the second residual block

rows.baseline: noisy model test performance (cyan dashed line in Figure 2)
rows.value: improves the noisy model’s performance substantially; further stitching results in performance at par with that of the noise-free model, irrespective of the r value.
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative improvement and parity, without exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The condition lists replacement through block two, but the value also includes parity obtained with further replacement. Separate these depths. Replacing only the earliest clean blocks does not improve performance. These results do not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: CNN model trained on SVHN
rows.stage_stated: trained on SVHN with varied fractions of randomly labeled training examples
rows.operation_detail: Stitched early layers of a noise-free model to deeper layers of a noisy model; evaluated test accuracy.

conditions.value: up to half the model’s depth

rows.baseline: noisy model test performance (cyan dashed line in Figure 2)
rows.value: The similar trend is observed for CNN model trained on noisy SVHN dataset.
rows.note: The text refers to the ResNet result’s trend, without giving exact values.
rows.check: The condition conflates the earliest replacements, which do not improve performance, with replacement through approximately half the model, which does. The CNN finding is qualitative and does not measure a listed version.
